summary: Takashi Maeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied in the doctoral program at Tohoku University (~1967–1973). He later held posts as a lecturer at Taisho University, attested in 1995 and 2006.

Takashi Nakao (1931–2020) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Rissho University (~1955–1957) and Tokyo University of Education (-1974), later serving at Bunkyo University Women's College (~1966–1971), Rissho University (1979–2002), and the Society of Japanese Historical Documents.

Takashi Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1979–1990), Peking University (1986–1989), and the University of Tokyo (-2009), and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University from 1991.

Takashi Yamada is a researcher in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Hosei University (~1973–1977) and served as an assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (~1998–2005).
Takatoshi Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University, attested in 1981 and 1991.
Takatoshi Nakamura worked in Buddhist studies and studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He was attested as a researcher at the Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute, Taisho University, in 1978.

Takatsugu Hayashi works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Delhi (attested 1996). His posts include Tohoku University, Sendai National College of Technology, Hosen Gakuen College, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takayasu Higuchi (1919–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942). He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1964–1983) and directed several research institutes and museums.

Takayasu Kimura is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. In 1995, he was attested as a lecturer at Taisho University and a researcher at the Institute of Modern Religious Education of Shingon Buzan.
Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1983–1993). He became a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University around 2011.

Takayoshi Kamei (1886–1977) specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1908–1911). He held positions at the University of Tokyo (~1916–1951), Ibaraki University (~1951–1961), and Seisen University (~1961–1974).

Takayoshi Namikawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies and doctorate at Bukkyo University (~1969–1996), where he became a professor in 1981 and emeritus professor in 2018, alongside a visiting post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1989–1990).

Takayuki Hirosawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held appointments at Taisho University, serving as a group member through 1991 and as a professor attested in 2014.

Takehiro Sueki (1921–2007) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944). He held posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1954–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino (1914–2007) specialized in history, archaeology, and Sinology, studying at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He held posts at Kyoto University (1936–1977), followed by professorships at Otemon Gakuin University (1977) and Otemae University (1980), where he served as president.

Takeo Kanaseki (1897–1983) worked in history and archaeology after studying at Kyoto University (~1919–1923). He held academic posts at Kyushu University (~1949–1960), Tottori University (~1960–1969), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1969–1979).

Takeshi Fujii specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi (~1976–1986) before serving at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as assistant, lecturer, professor (2001, 2009), and emeritus professor (2021).

Takeshi Hasegawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Ryukoku University (attested 1998) and served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Takeshi Karashima (1903–1967) was a Sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1924–1927). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1928–1945), Kamakura's library (~1947–1950), Sagami Women's University (~1951–1967), and Showa Women's University.

Takeshi Umehara (1925–2019) worked in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies, studying at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi (1945–1948). He held posts at Ryukoku, Ritsumeikan, Kyoto City University of Arts, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, and the Institute of Technologists.
